messages:
eng-oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cb-runtime-prod high error-rate and tail latency spike detected. Metric: continuous_batch_queue_length >> 95th pct, kv_cache_evictions skyrocketing. Auto-remediation attempted: scaled-pools. See https://metrics/redwood/cb-prod/2790012345
olivia: i’m on it, paging pagerduty and grabbing latest traces. rough impact?
sam: seeing sustained queueing, continuous-batching queues piling. microbatch sizes growing to ~512 on some requests, causing kv cache churn. a few 503s from backend pools.
kevin: rolling metrics look like sudden increase in `kv_cache.miss_rate` and eviction storms -> cache thrash. probably a workload that has many unique prefixes suddenly. also jitter in per-worker batching timer.
maria: we have 3 customer tickets calling about timeouts on embeddings/longchat. CS flagged two paying customers in EU region.
emily: customer note: they say requests started failing ~5m ago, some timeouts then 502s. SLA sensitivity.
olivia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cap microbatch size to 64, 2) lower batch window to 10ms, 3) enable aggressive kv eviction threshold flag (feature-flag: runtime.kv_aggressive_eviction=true) on affected pool. who can flip?
kevin: i can push flags to the cb-worker pool in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. will do staged: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
sam: while kevin does that, i’ll pin a fallback model variant with smaller context (model-x-small) for high concurrency routes to reduce kv pressure.
olivia: also enable `cache.prefix_sharing=true` temporary? that reduces distinct prefix keys for streaming sessions. any risk?
kevin: prefix_sharing reduces accuracy for some structured outputs, but for mitigation it's fine. enabling on canary now: `./infra/ff-toggle --env prod --flag runtime.prefix_sharing --on --pool cb-usw2-canary`
eng-oncall-bot: Deploy started: runtime.prefix_sharing canary in cb-usw2-canary by kevin at 2790012400.
kevin: pushed microbatch cap config to canary: `microbatch.max_tokens=64` and `batching.window_ms=10`. monitoring.
sam: pinned fallback model on routing config: `route: /v1/chat -> fallback: model-x-small (10%)` to start. will increase if stable.
maria: logged customer incidents and notified account teams for the two EU customers. asking for estimated degradation window to share.
olivia: initial effect: queue length down 30% on canary nodes, eviction rate down 45% on canary. latency 95p improved a bit. will continue roll.
kevin: ramping to 50% now. applying kv_aggressive_eviction on 50%: `infra apply --pool cb-usw2-1,cb-euw1-1 --set runtime.kv_aggressive_eviction=true`
sam: seeing transient 502 spike during rollout in one AZ (probably connection churn). fallback routing handled most requests.
eng-oncall-bot: Notice: automated alert cleared for canary pools at 2790012530 (eviction rate normalized on canaries).
emily: support update: customers still seeing intermittent timeouts but far reduced. sending update to accounts with interim mitigation status.
maria: CS asked for ETA to full mitigation. any estimate?
kevin: if ramp continues without further regressions, full rollout in ~12 min. still watching memory pressure on workers.
olivia: can we also tighten continuous-batch throttle on public routes? e.g. reduce per-connection inflight windows to limit request fanout.
sam: added throttle: `cb.throttle.inflight_per_conn=4` across edge proxies. should stop some pathological clients. deploy queued.
eng-oncall-bot: Throttle deploy started at 2790012720 by sam.
kevin: full rollout complete at 2790012920. microbatch cap + window + aggressive eviction + prefix_sharing + throttle all live. final metrics: queue length down 78% cluster-wide, eviction rate down 70%, 95p latency down 60% vs peak.
olivia: customer impact: estimated 10-15 minutes of degraded p95/p99 for a small subset of customers, with short 502/503s during roll. CS can send final wrap note.
emily: composing message now. getting approval from legal for wording.
maria: tracking followups: 1) postmortem to include root cause analysis, 2) permanent configs and tradeoff analysis for prefix_sharing, 3) improved trigger and runbook for kv-thrash scenarios.
sam: root cause notes: sudden workload shift from new customer integration generating many unique streaming prefixes + a timer jitter bug in batching window algorithm that allowed microbatches to grow unbounded under high concurrency. interactions caused kv cache to thrash (evictions -> cold misses -> larger batches -> more keys).
kevin: we should backport a fix to batching timer to ensure max_batch_interval applies under high concurrency scenarios. I'll open PR with deterministic test. also propose adding `kv_cache.eviction_slow_start` to rate-limit eviction ramp.
olivia: handoff: i’ll leave a summary for next on-call (morning shift). Handoff notes: mitigations used, rollback plan (revert flags `runtime.prefix_sharing=false` & remove microbatch caps) only after load validated for 2 hours.
eng-oncall-bot: page created: PD-9471 (high kv cache evictions -> cb perf cliff). severity: high. assigned to olivia.
emily: final customer update sent at 2790013120.
maria: ticketing: postmortem task created and assigned. linking PD-9471 and support tickets.
olivia: thanks everyone. if you touched configs, please add exact diffs to PD-9471 so we can audit. I’ll draft the incident timeline and postmortem template tonight. :thumbsup:
